extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of American government/public administration; policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for designing, staffing, and overseeing the national executive (President, Cabinet, and departments) in a representative government; addresses appointment, tenure, competence, party relations, and legislative oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential training and administrative experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration is something that men must learn, not something to be born. ... there can be found in the official systems of the States a lower grade of service in which men may advantageously be drilled for Presidential functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers selection of Presidents with preparatory training/experience (e.g., experienced state governors). Advocates training-schools / apprenticeship through minor offices so that executives are prepared rather than merely talented by instinct. Anti-pattern: treating the Presidency as something any shrewd man can take up without prior administrative experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of service and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Short terms which cut off the efficient as surely and inexorably as the inefficient are quite as repugnant to republican as to monarchical rules of wisdom. A President is dismissed almost as soon as he has learned the duties of his office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer continuity in office (or mechanisms to retain experienced administrators) is favorable to efficient administration; short elective terms that remove effective officers quickly are criticized as undermining competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of Secretaries' character and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The characters and training of the Secretaries are of almost as much importance as his [the President's] own gifts and antecedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment and Senate confirmation of Secretaries are integral to creating a working executive; selecting officers with proper character and training is essential because they are 'integral parts' of the branch and materially shape administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cabinet coherence depends on presidential leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the President was to take the advice of his appointees and colleagues appears to have depended always upon the character and temper of the President. ... There is no influence except the ascendency or tact of the President himself to keep a Cabinet in harmony and to dispose it to cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cabinet independence and harmony cannot be prescribed by fixed rules; effective joint responsibility and cooperation largely depend on the President's personal leadership, tact, and ascendancy. Anti-pattern: expecting uniform cabinet cohesion irrespective of presidential style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental heads must be competent and have integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: No President, however earnest and industrious, can keep the Navy in a state of creditable efficiency if he have a corrupt or incapable Secretary in the Navy Department; he cannot prevent the army from suffering the damage of demoralization if the Secretary of War is without either ability, experience, or conscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence and probity of Secretaries are crucial—failures by department heads produce concrete damage across their portfolios (Navy, War, Justice, Interior, State, Treasury examples). Selecting capable, experienced, and conscientious heads is essential to functional administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical expertise over partisan appointment for administrative roles
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of the utmost importance that a Secretary ... should be carefully chosen from amongst men skilled in financial administration and experienced in business regulation; but it is no more necessary that the man selected ... should be an active politician ... than it is to have a strictly political officer to fulfill his other duty of prescribing game laws for Alaska.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For offices whose functions are primarily administrative or technical (e.g., Treasury), priority should be given to domain expertise and administrative skill rather than partisan spoils. Anti-pattern: using technical departmental posts as purely partisan spoils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent civil service exerts substantial control
rubrics_metrics.description: They [Secretaries] differ from the permanent officials only in not being permanent. The permanent organization, the clerical forces of the departments, have in the Secretaries a sort of sliding top; though it would probably be just as convenient in practice to have this lid permanent as to have it movable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes the real power and continuity often lie with permanent clerks and bureaus; policy and administration are materially affected by the civil service irrespective of changing political chiefs. Implication: reforms should account for the role of permanent staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing Committees of Congress direct much executive policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All the big affairs of the departments are conducted in obedience to the direction of the Standing Committees. ... In the actual control of affairs no one can do very much without gaining the ears of the Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative committees exercise thorough-going supervision and shape major policy; evaluating executive action must consider committee influence. Anti-pattern: treating the Cabinet as sole director of departmental policy in the face of powerful committee control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and defects of congressional oversight mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Its intercourse with the departments has no easier channels than private consultations ... informal interviews ... and the written correspondence which the cabinet officers ... address ... investigations ... do not afford it more than a glimpse of the inside of a small province of federal administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Congress has oversight intent, its practical tools (private consultations, correspondence, ad hoc investigations) are often insufficient to penetrate departmental workings; hostile officials can evade inquiries. Evaluations should account for these practical constraints on oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impeachment is an inadequate tool for managerial correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The processes of impeachment ... are ponderous and difficult to handle. ... impeachment may be said to be little more than an empty menace. ... Impeachment is aimed altogether above the head of business management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment addresses gross crimes and is impractical for routine managerial failures; for administrative inefficiency the appropriate remedy is dismissal rather than impeachment. Policy design should provide easier, proportionate means to remove inefficient officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for an authority able to dismiss for inefficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ultimate authority, whose privilege it shall be to dismiss for inefficiency. ... Dismissal is quite as effective for his purposes, and more merciful to the clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective administration requires an accessible mechanism to remove inefficient or incompetent officials (short of impeachment). The absence of such a mechanism is a serious inconvenience of the constitutional arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive as agent of legislative will; role clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: He [the executive] considered the executive magistracy as nothing more than an institution for carrying the will of the legislature into effect; that the person or persons who should constitute the executive ought to be appointed by, and accountable to, the legislature only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the executive's normative role as implementer of legislative decisions; policy appraisal should respect the primacy of legislative direction while assessing whether means exist to make that principle effective in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party divergence complicates effective party government
rubrics_metrics.description: This constant possibility of party diversity between the Executive and Congress which so much complicates our system of party government. The history of administrations is not necessarily the history of parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When different parties control the Presidency and Congress (or the two Houses), policy direction, accountability, and party government become complicated and less coherent; effective governance benefits from alignment between branches, or mechanisms to manage divergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cabinet's declining role as party leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cabinet has advanced in party insignificance as the system has grown older. ... as the Committees gained facility and power the leadership of the Cabinet lost ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical trend: early cabinets acted as party leaders, but over time legislative committees absorbed leadership functions; evaluations of modern cabinets should not assume they retain the party-authoritative role they once did.
